https://t.co/kgZeByAQj2 has now assembled five popular models into the same 90% OFF lineup:

🧠 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash

⚙️ GLM-5.3-Flash

💻 Qwen3.8-Flash

🤖 Hy3

🎨 MiMo-V2.5

Starting September 16 at 17:00 SGT, all five can be accessed through https://t.co/kgZeByAQj2 at 10% of their official standard pricing under the current offer.

The obvious story is the discount.

The more interesting story is what lower inference costs can change downstream.

AI applications do not pay for intelligence once.

They pay every time intelligence is used.

One user request might require one model call.

A coding Agent may require dozens.

A complex autonomous workflow may repeatedly reason, inspect context, call tools, evaluate results and continue until a task is complete.

📊 At sufficient scale, inference stops being a minor software expense.

It becomes part of the application's unit economics.

This is why a 90% reduction in model-call pricing can potentially affect more than the monthly AI bill.

It can change which workflows are economically practical.

A developer might allow an Agent to reason for longer.

A product might process more context.

A startup might serve more users before infrastructure costs become restrictive.

Experiments that were previously expensive may become cheap enough to test.

But there is another important dimension here.

https://t.co/kgZeByAQj2 is not discounting one model.

It is putting five different model families behind the same pricing tier.

🌐 That introduces optionality.

Developers do not necessarily need one universal model for every task.

They can potentially choose different intelligence for different workloads while keeping access inside the same infrastructure layer.

That matters because the cheapest model is not always the cheapest system.

A model that costs less per token but requires more calls, more retries or produces lower-quality outputs may ultimately cost more per successful task.

The more useful metric is often:

💰 Cost per completed workload.

Of course, promotional pricing should not be treated as permanent infrastructure economics unless its duration and future terms support that assumption.

Production teams still need to understand pricing conditions, model behavior, reliability and workload requirements.

But the direction is worth watching.

The AI race is no longer only about building more capable models.

It is increasingly about making capable intelligence economically deployable at scale.

And once model capability becomes abundant, the infrastructure that routes intelligence at the right cost may become just as strategically important as the models themselves. 🌐
